accuracy.evidence: Framing matches the DfE Health Education statutory guidance (2019), which by the end of primary expects pupils to recognise and talk about their emotions and to judge whether what they feel and how they behave is appropriate, and the EYFS Managing Self goal. The feeling/behaviour split and the stop-and-breathe pause follow the emotion regulation literature cited by the topic (Gross process model: the response is modulated after the emotion arises). No claim says feelings can be switched off; the text says you cannot always stop a feeling from coming.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the four mistakes adults meet at 6 to 8: a feeling is bad (Sam feels jealous judged OK, m8 asks how many times Sam was bad for feeling jealous), the feeling made me do it (Jo's I had to kick him, challenge options the feeling makes Pip do it and if the feeling is very big), confusing a doing with a feeling (shouting prediction, crying and running away options), and brave kids never feel scared.

lab_distinct.evidence: flagfeelact is built round the gap between a feeling and a doing: a feeling/doing card sort, a six-choice menu for one cross feeling, a feeling bubble and doing box with a dashed gap where a draggable STOP octagon must land before any choice appears, and an OK/Not OK judging deck. Highest 6-token shingle overlap with another flagship lab is 4.2% (flag_rights).

lab_teaches.evidence: The child discovers the rule by acting: the sort separates inside feelings from body doings, the menu shows one cross feeling allows six different doings, the pause step only offers the two choices after STOP is placed in the gap, and the judge deck makes feeling jealous and angry OK every time while breaking and kicking are never OK. Done messages state the rule only after the task.

predictions.evidence: Three predictions are locked before acting: is shouting a feeling or a doing (tempting: a feeling), how many things could cross Mia do (tempting: only one, hit something), what helps you choose when a feeling is big (tempting: do the first thing you think of), and is it wrong to feel jealous (tempting: yes). Each done message reports the prediction back.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Five rotating challenge questions with shuffled options; each wrong option has its own message, e.g. Angry is the feeling, a doing is something your body does; Brave people feel scared too; A feeling does not make you do anything, stop, breathe, then choose; Crying is a doing that shows a feeling. In the lab, each unkind menu choice has its own reason (kicking breaks things, hitting hurts, mean names hurt).

readability.evidence: Kid explanation is Flesch-Kincaid grade 1.7 and the adult text 5.9, inside the family targets of 5.0 and 10.0. Canvas words are short and concrete (cross, scared, stamp my feet, STOP), cards use 2 to 6 words, and the two key terms feeling and doing are taught first on their own intro step.

no_filler.evidence: Every paragraph carries a rule or an example: feelings happen inside you, doings are chosen, every feeling is OK, stop and breathe in the gap. No praise padding or throat-clearing; the explanation overlaps no other lesson above the 12% limit, including Simple Calming Strategies and Emotions and Decision-Making, which teach calming tools and choice under strong emotion for older children.

mobile.evidence: Screenshots at 360 px Android in light and dark: sort card, bins, six-choice grid, STOP gap row and OK/Not OK pads all fit with no clipping after the menu header emoji was moved left of the text so they no longer overlap. Tap targets are at least 58 px tall on canvas and duplicated as large buttons below; phone_sweep reports 0 findings on iPhone 13 and Android.

accessibility.evidence: walk.cjs: every task finishes with Show me on desktop and iPhone 13, and axe-core reports no WCAG 2.1 AA violations in light or dark theme. Every canvas action has a button twin with an aria-label (e.g. Cross is a feeling), feedback is spoken through the polite live region and the canvas aria-label, and the STOP gap can be filled by a single button tap instead of a drag.
